proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly distinguishes sūjī “needle, small awl”, from sūcikā, from the semolina and tailor homonyms. CDIAL 13551,1 includes sūcikā in its needle head as well as the contracted sūī family. The survey j/z forms therefore belong to this needle family, with the voiced medial consonant retained in the analysis. Regional learned or vernacular transfer remains unresolved; the link does not treat j as an arbitrary spelling of zero.

proposals.evidence: Full calati gives Hindi calnā, Mth calab, Bengali calā and Oriya caḷibā with the short-vowel cal stem. These central/eastern simple responses retain that stem with imperative or infinitive endings. Longer auxiliaries and the western cāl/call family, which Turner separately places under *calyati 4721, are not folded into this decision. The link identifies the family while retaining possible regional transfer, explicitly relevant to the eastern Hindi-type forms.
